`UnifiedActivationPipeline` (`.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js`) is the single entry point for all 12 agents. `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. `GreetingBuilder` assembles greetings with pre-loaded enriched context. `loadUserProfile()` runs in `buildGreeting()` and is passed to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid duplicate `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional `userProfile` for bob-mode restriction. PM bypasses that restriction; non-PM bob agents show redirect for `auto`, named greeting for forced `named`, and return empty commands. Pipeline: Phase 1, 5 parallel loaders (`Promise.all`); Phase 2, agent def; Phase 3, sequential preference/session type/workflow; Phase 4, enriched context; Phase 5, `GreetingBuilder`.

8 agents have command `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` lack visibility and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master` uses `visibility: full`. `*yolo` is universal across all 12 agents. Badge: `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` in `greeting-builder.js`.

Mock `resolveConfig` with `mockReturnValue` (not `mockReturnValueOnce`) when called multiple times. `validate-user-profile.js` `validateUserProfile()` is pure (no filesystem). Always mock `fs`, `js-yaml`, `config-resolver`, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. `resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) has highest priority. `user_profile` is `USER_FIELD` in `migrate-config.js`; `toggleUserProfile()` in `config-resolver.js` flips bob<->advanced.

`PermissionMode` and `OperationGuard` in `.aios-core/core/permissions/` are functional. `index.js` wires `cycleMode()` and `enforcePermission()`. Mode cycle: `explore`(0) -> `ask`(1) -> `auto`(2) -- `PermissionMode.MODE_CYCLE`.

Formats: structured (`name: xxx`) and compact (`key: 'value'`); compact agents are qa, devops, data-engineer, ux-design-expert. Always match existing format when editing. Source: `.aios-core/development/agents/`; Claude mirror: `.claude/commands/AIOS/agents/`. These are separate files; `ideSync` handles sync separately.

Use `fs.writeFile(path, data, { flag: 'wx' })` for exclusive-create lock; include PID + timestamp for stale detection. Stale threshold ~10s; timeout ~3s, polling 50ms. Temp file (`{path}.tmp.{pid}`) + `fs.rename()`; Windows rename fails if target exists, so fall back to direct `fs.writeFile()`. `.git/HEAD` mtime + `.git/index` mtime = cache fingerprint. Use `git rev-parse --git-dir` for worktree-aware git path and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to detect worktree vs main tree. For dual-purpose lock/cache `writeFile`, use broad `mockResolvedValue` and verify via `mock.calls` filtering. Mock `child_process.execSync` separately from `execa`. Use `jest.requireActual('fs')` for real filesystem checks in hook existence tests.

All section builders (`buildPresentation`, `buildRoleDescription`, `buildProjectStatus`, `buildFooter`, `buildContextSection`) accept optional `sectionContext`; `_buildContextualGreeting` builds it from enriched pipeline context and passes it to all builders. With context, presentation uses brief named greeting for existing/workflow sessions; without it, archetypal fallback (backward compatible). `_formatProjectStatusNarrative()` creates natural-language sentences; without context, legacy `_formatProjectStatus()` remains. `_safeBuildSection(fn)` wraps builders with SECTION_TIMEOUT (150ms) + try/catch. `Promise.all([contextSection, workflowSection])` parallelizes independent sections. Footer: new=`*guide`; existing=`*help + *session-info`; workflow=`Focused on **{story}**`. ACT-5 changes (lines 661-816 in greeting-builder.js) must NOT be touche
